title: Cutters, tearers and grinders: your teeth at work
examples: What are the different types of teeth?

groups.label: Incisors: cut
groups.ask: What are the different types of teeth?

explain.say: Take a big bite of an apple, then chew it. Did you notice different teeth doing different jobs? Your mouth is like a kitchen full of tools. Let's sort which teeth do which job.

draw.text: Cutters, tearers and grinders: your teeth at work

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: the layers of a tooth. Can you see the enamel and the dentine? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Cutters, tearers and grinders: your teeth at work

explain.say: See the Incisors lighting up? Incisors are your flat front teeth, eight of them, four on top and four below. They are sharp like scissors, so they cut and snip food, like biting an apple. Can you feel their sharp edges with your tongue?

groups.label: Incisors: cut
groups.ask: What are the different types of teeth?

explain.say: Now the Canines glow. Canines are the four pointy teeth next to your incisors. They grip and tear chewy food, like naan or dried mango. Look in a mirror: can you find your pointy canines?

groups.label: Incisors: cut
groups.ask: What are the different types of teeth?

explain.say: Here are the Molars, the big, wide teeth at the back. Molars grind and mash food into a soft paste, like a grinding stone, so you can swallow it. Chew some rice and feel which teeth are working hardest.

groups.label: Incisors: cut
groups.ask: What are the different types of teeth?

explain.say: Now look inside one tooth. See the enamel shining on top? Enamel is the hard, white coat that protects the tooth, and inside are dentine and a soft pulp. Great job! Wow fact: enamel is the hardest thing in your whole body, even harder than bone.

faq.q: What are the different types of teeth?
faq.a: There are incisors at the front for cutting, pointy canines for tearing, and wide premolars and molars at the back for grinding. A grown-up usually has 32 teeth and a child has 20 baby teeth.
asks: How many teeth do we have?

faq.a: Molars are the big, flat-topped teeth at the back of your mouth. They grind and crush food into small pieces so it is easy to swallow.
Enamel is the hard, white outer coat of a tooth. It is the hardest substance in the human body, but sugar acids can still wear holes in it.
Under the enamel is dentine, a yellowish layer. In the middle is the pulp, with nerves and blood vessels, which is why a deep hole can hurt.
Canines are pointy so they can grip and tear food. Meat-eating animals like lions and dogs have very long canines.

facts: Tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body.
Children have 20 baby teeth; adults usually have 32 permanent teeth, including wisdom teeth.

quiz.say: Which teeth grind your food at the back of your mouth?
quiz.show: The grinding teeth at the back are…
quiz.why: Molars are wide, back teeth that grind food.

wrong.0: Incisors are at the front for cutting.
wrong.1: Canines are pointy teeth for tearing.

quiz.say: What is the hard, white outer coat of a tooth called?
quiz.show: The hard, white coat of a tooth is…
quiz.why: Enamel is the hard outer coat that protects the tooth.

wrong.0: The pulp is the soft centre with nerves.
